status_summary: As of 2026-10-07 the administration has a published plan that moves in the Mandate's direction but has not implemented it. The FEMA Review Council created by EO 14180 (2025-01-24) issued its final report dated 2026-05-07 (dhs.gov, 75 pages), with ten recommendations, among them: resetting the Public Assistance per capita indicator for 1986 to 1999 inflation, from 1.94 to 2.99 dollars (about 16 fewer major declarations a year, by its estimate), and reverting Individual Assistance criteria to pre-2019 factors, threshold changes it says would require regulation, plus an annual minimum state expenditure before a declaration request; replacing the Hazard Mitigation Grant Program with a two-phase state-managed program at a 50 to 75 percent federal share tied to state performance; a single direct Individual Assistance payment; direct Public Assistance funding (RAPID); NFIP reform (CRS In Focus IF13302 of 2026-08-28 reads this as a gradual move of certain policies to private insurers through a voluntary take-out program under existing authorities, a marketplace evaluation and continued Risk Rating 2.0 pricing, and quotes the Council as acknowledging that legislation would be required); and a transformed agency that retains FEMA's core missions as a payer of last resort (CRS also reports that it keeps the Emergency Management Performance Grant). No recommendation to move the agency out of DHS, or to Interior, was found, and the Council advocates legislative action for a sustained transformation. No rule, order or law implementing it was found: the Federal Register shows only routine inflation adjustments to per capita indicators (2026-04-28 and 2026-09-29), and the House committee advanced H.R. 4669 in September 2025 with no Senate companion. On grants, FEMA canceled the BRIC mitigation program in April 2025 (about 3.6 billion dollars), a federal judge ordered it restored in December 2025 and March 2026, and FEMA reopened applications on 2026-03-25 under new criteria.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14180 establishes a FEMA Review Council, with a report due within 180 days of its first meeting and a one-year term unless extended; CRS says later orders moved the report deadline to no later than 2026-05-29.
FEMA publishes a Federal Register notice of the establishment of the FEMA Review Council.

Executive Order 14239 sets a federalism policy for preparedness and orders a National Resilience Strategy, policy reviews and a federal functions framework; it contains no cost-share or per-capita threshold changes.
Secretary Noem says at a Cabinet meeting that DHS will move to eliminate FEMA; Semafor notes closing the agency requires an act of Congress.

FEMA cancels the Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities (BRIC) mitigation grant program, affecting about 3.6 billion dollars in projects (month known only; first of month used). A judge later orders it restored (December 2025 and March 2026).

DHS says FEMA will limit Disaster Relief Fund activity to immediate threats to life, health or safety during the funding lapse; roughly four days later FEMA releases about 5 billion dollars. E&E News reported on 2026-02-27 that funding for ongoing and legacy disasters had been halted and allocations of 100,000 dollars or more were under review.

FEMA opens applications for 1 billion dollars in new BRIC funding for fiscal years 2024 and 2025 after court orders from U.S. District Judge Stearns in a suit by 22 states and the District of Columbia; new rules end funding for hazard mitigation planning and cap awards per recipient.

FEMA notice sets the statewide per capita indicator for recommending cost share adjustments at 189 dollars for major disasters declared in 2026; a 2026-09-29 notice raises the countywide indicator under the same inflation-adjustment practice. No larger threshold increase, deductible or cost-share change was found.

The FEMA Review Council's final report, dated 2026-05-07 and posted on dhs.gov, makes ten recommendations, including an inflation reset of the Public Assistance per capita indicator from 1.94 to 2.99 dollars, minimum state spending before declaration requests, replacement of the Hazard Mitigation Grant Program with a two-phase program at a 50 to 75 percent federal share tied to state performance, a single direct Individual Assistance payment, direct Public Assistance funding (RAPID), NFIP reform and a transformed agency that retains FEMA's core missions. These are recommendations; the Council advocates legislative action for durable change.

title: Shift disaster costs to states; wind down NFIP and most FEMA preparedness grants
uncertainties: The Council's final report was read from a copy retrieved from dhs.gov on 2026-10-26 (75 pages); the address still refuses automated fetches, and page references come from the reading of that copy. Page 2 is a placeholder for a co-chair letter, so the report carries no transmittal letter or signer. The implementation table on printed page 15 is a graphic: its text layer holds only the introduction (the minimum action required, with the Council advocating legislative action), and the reading that recommendations 4, 5, 6, 7 and 10 need legislation (10 also an executive order), 3 regulation, 8 an executive order, 1 and 9 policy, and 2 policy and regulation comes from a visual reading of the graphic only and was not verified from the text. The 29 percent, 1.5 billion dollar and 113 million dollar figures are the report's own back-cast estimates, not observed outcomes. Reported but not verified: that the report calls its recommendations nonbinding, that public comment on the report closed on 2026-06-08, that the Council backed off proposed staffing cuts (CRS cites a news report; the report itself calls for a staffing review over two to three years), a 150,000 dollar individual payment figure from an association summary, CRS's statement that the report keeps the Emergency Management Performance Grant, and an earlier lead that FEMA lost about one-fifth of its staff by July 2025. Whether any executive order, rule or guidance has implemented the report since 2026-05-07 was not found in a Federal Register search of presidential documents; FEMA press releases and reporting from June to October 2026 were not checked, so the absence of implementing action rests on a limited search. The FEMA press release of 2026-05-07 failed to load. The BRIC cancellation date (April 2025) and court order months come from one PBS report without exact days. Stage 'proposed' is a judgment: the BRIC cancellation was operative for several months before the court order, so a reader could argue for in_progress. Searches run: FEMA Review Council final report; BRIC, preparedness grants and NFIP; plus Federal Register queries for per capita indicators and FEMA presidential documents.
